Question: Were Siths ever trained really young the way Jedis are trained?
Answer: In Canon and Legends, training children in the way of the Sith was both encouraged and prohibited depending upon which Sith organization was in charge Maul, for example in Canon, was stolen by Sidious at a young age from his Mother Talzin and trained in the ways of the Sith. “Sidious promised to make me his right hand, but instead, he stole what was most dear to me... my own flesh and blood. -Mother Talzin discussing her son Maul and Sidious Mother Talzin and her son Maul In Canon, Maul was taken by Sidious and beaten daily by two Nightbrothers chosen by Sidious. Maul was abused so badly daily, he could barely stand. Anger and rage festered in Maul just as Sidious had planned and wanted. In Legends, during Maul’s first year of birth, his Morher Talzin, persuaded Darth Sidious to take her son and train him in the ways of the Darkside. Maul was taken to Mustafar and trained by droids vigorously and savagely. Sith Academy In Legends, during some time periods Initiates were taken as children and trained in the ways of the Sith in institutions. But during other times, the Sith frowned upon training the very young, preferring to take an Apprentice, when they are older and more powerful in the Force. Sith Empire During the time of the Sith Empire, Force sensitive children were forcibly taken from their parents, and placed in Sith academic institutions. Darth Bane Darth Bane changed all that when he instituted the Rule of Two. Bane taught and preferred taking Apprentices that were older and not children. The Legends book, Darth Plagueis explained the rationale and reasoning why under the Rule of Two, Sith Apprentices were not chosen from children. “For the past five hundred years, the Sith of the Bane line had eschewed selecting children as apprentices, finding it more advantageous to discover beings who had already been hardened or scarred by life.” Darth Bane’s Apprentice Darth Zannah Darth Bane and those that followed preferred Sith Apprentices who had been scarred and beaten down by life before taking them as Apprentices. The Sith Empire instead preferred to fester that anger and hatred themselves by making their child Initiates suffer by their own hands. It is understandable why Bane changed the age when Apprentices were taken. The Rule of Two was based upon two full fledged Sith, one who has the power and one who craves it. To train an Apprentice to desire to overthrow their Master required an Apprentice that possessed the maturity and the power to do such an act. The Rule of Two was also based upon secrecy and subterfuge. Imperial Army of the Sith Empire During the time of the Sith Empire, the Sith was more like a military order and needed the large number of Sith shock troops to wage their wars across the galaxy. This required training from a very early age by a large number of Force sensitive children. Though in Legends, other Sith Lords broke this rule and trained their Apprentices from childhood. Darth Tenebrous convinced Hego Damask II’s parents to allow him to take their child and train him in the ways of Sith. Hego would eventually become Darth Plageuis. Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plageuis Plageuis in turn convinced a boy named Palpatine and convinced the latter to kill his family. Once that was done, Plageuis took Palpatine as a child as his Apprentice. So in conclusion, during some time periods, Sith were trained as children, and during other time periods, it was strictly forbidden, though the rule was often broken. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: What DC Universe sci-fi alien metal is resistant to lightsabers?
Answer: Well there are a number of materials in the DC Universe that would be resistant to lightsabers and some are alien There are some that are pre-and Post crisis some that are Post 52, but I will discuss a different number of them. Supermanium According to Superman, he forged it out of the heart of a star and it formed a metallic substance that is as indestructible as Superman yet does not have any weakness to magic. Amazonium In the Pre-Crisis Universe, Amazonium was an indestructible metal from Wonder Woman’s home island that was made stronger by a spell from Aphrodite, and let her bracelets repel everything from bullets to energy blasts. Wonder Woman’s bracelets, Tiara and Lasso were made of Amazonium. The only things that could damage it were magical weapons. It first appeared and was named in Wonder Woman #52. Now her bracelets are made of an unknown but powerful metal. Nth metal Nth metal is from the Planet Thanagar and is used by Thanagarian race of people. It has many amazing properties including the ability to negate gravity and help its wielders fly. But much like vibranium, Nth metal is extremely strong, durable, and somewhat rare in its supply, but has also been known to hold abilities that for see anything that vibranium is capable of. Able to effectively protect its user from deadly environmental conditions, act as a formidable weapon, absorb energy, literally morph its shape according to the situation at hand, negate magic, and even warp reality if used properly. Marvelium Way back in Captain Marvel Adventure #100, Dr. Sivana went back in time to steal the mystic bracelet of the wizard Shazam, making himself a ghost who Captain Marvel couldn't touch. He went on to create a series of evil clones to fight him, so Captain Marvel created the new metal, marvelium. Marvelium is one of the world's strongest metals, so strong that only Captain Marvel himself can mold and shape it. It's also impenetrable, even to mystic beings. There are probably more that I’m forgetting but these DC alien Sci Fi metallic substances that could resist and block a lightsaber. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: As a Star Wars fan, would you prefer a new Rey movie directed by Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy or a Quinlan Vos movie based on the novel Dark Disciple or the Dark Horse Republic comics directed by an experience director?
Answer: I’d rather see a Quinlan Vos movie based on the novel Dark Disciple That book is one of my favorite Star Wars folks of all time, and actually one of my favorite books of all time. That book made Quinlan Vos one of my favorite characters and made me love Asajj Ventress. So many Star Wars books are devoid of any real growth or change in their characters. One of the many books with stagnant characters The books main characters are usually stagnant and frozen in time so as not to upset their portrayal in any movie. But Dark Disciple was different. Its story was incredibly compelling, and the main characters did grow and change a lot and the ending was incredible as well. It’s just a special book and should be read by any Star Wars fan and I think turning it into a movie would be absolutely fantastic. Christie Golden did a tremendous job writing the book but even she was gifted the stories from Favreau and Filoni since they were originally meant to be part of the Clone Wars and animated series. If a gifted director, hell even Zack Snyder, were allowed to bring this book to the big screen it would be amazing. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: Isn't it a little too much that in Ahsoka’s first episode Baylan Skoll and Hati bested a whole ship full of people? They are way OP in my opinion.
Answer: No, Jedi are trained from an early age to use their lightsabers as an extension of themselves and by the time that they are full-fledged Jedi, they have been blocking laser blasts their entire lives Remember this scene from the Prequels when Yoda is shown training Younglings? Or do you remember when Luke blocked these lasers with the blast shield on when he hardly had any training at all? Younglings, Padawans and Jedi all practiced the ability to use the Force and to block lasers from the moment, they first held a Lightsaber. Every single Force User we have seen has easily blocked lasers and taken out large numbers of non Force Users quite easily. Even the weakest of its members did this with ease. Baylan Skoll had been a Jedi for many years and by the time of the events of Ahsoka, he had been blocking lasers and fending off larger numbers of enemies for most of his life. It is literally second nature to him. Shin Hati was presumably, never a Jedi because she’s too young, but has obviously trained in the Master/Apprentice relationship with Skoll for many years. It is quite reasonable to assume that, as soon as she exhibited powers with the force that she has trained with a Lightsaber and learned to deflect blaster fire. And even if she didn’t learn and train to do that until much later, she still had many years to be trained by Baylon who is obviously a gifted Force User. She also seems to quite strong in the Force like her Master. Baylan is so powerful he bested Ahsoka in a lightsaber duel, which is incredibly impressive. So if you think the two of them are overpowered then you must have the same notions and feelings about all the Jedi. And if that’s so then you probably shouldn’t be watching Star Wars. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Why are Vader and Anakin spoken like totally different individuals that don't share anything?
Answer: Because according to Darth Vader, Anakin Skywalker died from his injuries on Mustafar and Vader was born in his stead Once he was encased in his armor, Darth Vader truly believed Anakin died on Mustafar, the same place he was born. Vader believed at that moment that he ceased to be Anakin and only Vader remained. Vader felt this way for most of his existence, that he was a completely different person. Or at least he tried to convince himself that. Vader knew deep down he was still Anakin because he was still haunted by Anakin’s memories. He desperately wanted them to be different people, in his mind he killed Anakin and rose as something stronger. However he was always aware of his past. And after the fall of the Republic and the decimation of the Jedi Order, most believed Anakin had perished with them. When Palpatine assumed complete control of his new Empire, he introduced Darth Vader as his second in command and was the will and the hand of the Emperor. Most didn’t know that Skywalker became Vader, and even those that did, accepted that the two were essentially different people(except for his son Luke). Of course, Luke proved that there was still good in Vader and as hard as he tried, Vader could never completely destroy Anakin. I hope that clears up any confusion!
